# Datastar sends a GET request's signals in the datastar query parameter (JSON,
# URL-encoded), since a GET request has no body. Under --output-datastar the
# signals argument on a GET route reads that parameter and unmarshals it into
# the parameter's type; an absent or malformed parameter answers 400, as a
# malformed body does on other methods.

muxt generate --output-datastar --use-receiver-type=Server
muxt check

exec go test -count=1

-- template.gohtml --
{{- define "GET /count Count(ctx, signals)" -}}{{- .Result -}}{{- end -}}
-- go.mod --
module server

go 1.24
-- template.go --
package server

import (
	"context"
	"embed"
	"html/template"
)

//go:embed *.gohtml
var templatesFS embed.FS

var templates = template.Must(template.ParseFS(templatesFS, "*"))

type Signals struct {
	Count int `json:"count"`
}

type Server struct{}

func (Server) Count(_ context.Context, signals Signals) (int, error) { return signals.Count, nil }
-- template_test.go --
package server

import (
	"net/http"
	"net/http/httptest"
	"net/url"
	"testing"
)

func TestSignalsOnGet(t *testing.T) {
	mux := http.NewServeMux()
	TemplateRoutes(mux, Server{})

	for _, tt := range []struct {
		name     string
		query    string
		wantCode int
		wantBody string
	}{
		{name: "valid", query: "?datastar=" + url.QueryEscape(`{"count":2}`), wantCode: http.StatusOK, wantBody: "2"},
		{name: "absent", query: "", wantCode: http.StatusBadRequest},
		{name: "malformed", query: "?datastar=" + url.QueryEscape("not-json"), wantCode: http.StatusBadRequest},
	} {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			rec := httptest.NewRecorder()
			mux.ServeHTTP(rec, httptest.NewRequest(http.MethodGet, "/count"+tt.query, nil))
			if rec.Code != tt.wantCode {
				t.Fatalf("status = %d, want %d", rec.Code, tt.wantCode)
			}
			if tt.wantBody != "" && rec.Body.String() != tt.wantBody {
				t.Errorf("body = %q, want %q", rec.Body.String(), tt.wantBody)
			}
		})
	}
}
